audit_items.proof_trace: The dedup cache at line 113 uses only (slot, proposerIndex) as the cache key, not including the block signature. When a cache hit occurs at line 113, the function returns ValidationIgnore at line 124 WITHOUT executing signature verification, allowing an attacker to submit a block with the same slot/proposer but an invalid or malicious signature that bypasses cryptographic verification.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker observes a legitimate block B1 from proposer P at slot S. Before B1 is marked as seen, attacker crafts a malicious block B2 with same (slot=S, proposer=P) but different signature and body. If attacker's B2 arrives first and passes initial dedup at line 113 (cache miss), it gets validated including signature check. Once B2 is in cache, legitimate B1 arrives and hits cache at line 113, returning ValidationIgnore without verifying B1's signature. The equivocation detection at line 115 only triggers if both blocks are from same slot/proposer AND one is already the head block, which may not occur if B2 is malicious and rejected later in the pipeline.
